correctness.rationale: A tagged coupon has Bin(t,p_N) counts; its fixed-c defect tail is q_N^t(tp_N/q_N)^{c−1}/(c−1)! times (1+O(1/t)), establishing logarithmic centering and the ratio q_N. For r tagged coupons, per-round no-hit probability q_N^r(1+O_r(1/N)), and separate single hits dominate the bounded-degree generating coefficient, yielding factorial moments m_N(t)^r(1+o(1)) at t=b_N+k. Binomial-product conditioning gives pairwise nonpositive defect covariance, so Var(U)≤EU; together with the union bound and geometric defect-ratio tails this gives uniform integrability of squares, lattice CDF and stated mean/variance series. Independent exact enumeration at N=4,d=2,c=2,t=2 yielded U-count frequencies {2:6,3:24,4:6}/36 and mean U=3, equal N P(Bin(2,1/2)≤1). Independent finite tests do not prove asymptotics.

originality.rationale: Schilling–Henze (2021) Theorem 2.1 proves fixed-s group-drawing Poisson limits at t=(N/s)(log N+(c−1)loglog N+...), a centering that is WRONG when s/N→rho>0 because the correct rate is −log(1−rho). The candidate proves the nonvanishing-fraction lattice regime, exact phase-dependent full CDF, repeated-coverage for each fixed c and o(1) mean/variance expansions. Berend–Sher covers macroscopic first-copy means but not full phase-resolved all-fixed-c law; a separate same-date published result concerns c growing like α log N, mathematically distinct. Historical general occupancy theorems remain a residual risk.
